summary: Six messages, two exchanges, and one thing that should not have happened. After 18 days of silence Mica reappeared on Aug 31 with a nudge about consistent posting and a single example reel — not the usual 7-10 link inspo drop, but it was the first proactive touch on this account in over two weeks, and it worked: Callie broke a 14-day silence within two minutes and answered warmly. Her reply is the most valuable line of the week and the first thing she has said about her Instagram since Jul 8: 'I'm using my back up account atm while I wait to get my bigger account back but I aim to post 3x a day'. That is confirmation, from the client, that the suspension she raised on Jun 23 is still unresolved 73 days later, that her main page is still gone, and that she is doing her own posting three times a day while the ALTR programme Derrek paused on Aug 1 remains dark. Nobody from ALTR responded to that disclosure at all — Mica replied 'amazing! 🤍' and the topic closed. Then on Sep 1 Stephski issued the Aug 15-31 invoice, on cadence, and did it while both previous cycles are still unreconciled to the client: the Aug 17 wire (18 days, sent against an account number changed mid-relationship, never confirmed) and the Jul 15-31 duplicate check she asked for on Aug 8 (27 days unanswered after 'Will update you shortly!'). This week's invoice also added a condition none of the previous four carried — 'I ask that you please pay within 7 days to avoid any pausing of work' — and skipped the pre-invoice heads-up that made the last cycle the smoothest of the relationship. Callie replied 'Thank youuu x'. Derrek has now been silent 34 days, Vivek has been in the chat 37 days without ever posting, Michelle has been silent 18 days with 48 client videos still unacknowledged, and 'crystalmila.vip' remains unexplained 12 days on.

health.rationale: Down 4 from 54, the smallest drop in four weeks, and the slide slowed only because of the client, not because of ALTR. Genuine positives: she broke a 14-day silence, replied within two minutes, engaged warmly twice, and volunteered that she is posting 3x a day on her own — this is not a client who has checked out. Mica also restarted contact after two missed weeks. Against that, the one thing last week's file named as the escalation event happened exactly as predicted: a third invoice went out on Sep 1 on top of two unreconciled payments, with no receipt confirmation, no answer to the 27-day-old duplicate question, no statement of which account the Aug 17 wire hit, and no pre-invoice heads-up — plus a new pay-or-work-pauses condition aimed at a client who has paid every invoice ever issued, on time, without dispute. Meanwhile she told the chat her main Instagram is still gone and nobody from ALTR acknowledged it: no Derrek (34 days), no Vivek (37 days, never spoken), no Michelle (18 days, 48 videos untouched). The account is now in the worst configuration available — a client who is still willing to talk, being met by a team that only speaks to invoice her.
